gloss: competitive; hating to lose; determined not to be beaten

definitions.explanation: A personality trait characterized by refusing to give up and striving to win or succeed. Generally seen as a positive quality in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い⟦だから→だから：00924_dakara⟧⟦{絶対|ぜったい}→絶対：00435_zettai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{諦|あきら}めない→諦める：01813_akirameru⟧。
examples.english: Because I hate losing, I never give up.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{頃|ころ}→ころ：03091_koro⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: I've been competitive since I was a child.

notes:
{負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い describes someone who cannot stand to come off worse — in a game, an argument, an exam, or just a comparison. It is a standing character trait, not a mood, so it is normally predicated of a person or a ⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧ rather than of a single occasion.

Formation: ⟦{負|ま}けず→負ける：01134_makeru⟧ 'not losing' (a literary negative of ⟦{負|ま}ける→負ける：01134_makeru⟧) + ⟦{嫌|きら}い→嫌い：02871_kirai⟧ 'dislike' — literally 'hating not to win'. The apparent double negative is a historical quirk; the meaning is simply 'hates losing'.

As a na-adjective it takes な before a noun:
- {負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧: a competitive person
- {負|ま}けず{嫌|ぎら}い⟦な→な：09497_na⟧⟦{性格|せいかく}→性格：03371_seikaku⟧: a competitive streak

The word is usually approving or at worst affectionate — it suggests drive and persistence, and is a stock compliment for athletes and hard-working students. To criticise the same trait a speaker would reach for something else, such as 'a sore loser'.

Compare ⟦{勝|か}ち{気|き}→勝ち気：07468_kachiki⟧, a near synonym focused on the wish to win rather than the dislike of losing, and used more often of women in older writing.
